title: Chapter 128: Stray Cat
html:
“Disappearance of the hospital director and patients. An anonymous letter claims that there are bodies left in the hospital.”

“A bloody message that changes by itself. Moans from a sealed room. Who opened the locked doors at midnight?”

“What have they seen to cause them to go crazy in one night? Who is the patient, and who is the doctor?”

“Screaming, cutting, sewing—the corruption of human nature in a hospital where the sun never rises.”

A glance at the headlines quickened Liu Dao’s pulse and made his breathing uneven. “Are you certain about this?”

Before coming, he had prepared multiple proposals and negotiating tactics, expecting Chen Ge to object over pay or safety. Now he realized the conversation had never been under his control.

The Haunted House owner not only ignored safety but complained that their locations looked fake, then chose an abandoned hospital whose search results alone were terrifying.

Is this man insane?Liu Dao’s smile froze. “Mr. Chen, our staff may not be willing to enter the location you chose. If you dislike the script, we can revise it.”

“It’s alright.” Chen Ge waved him off.

“Thank you for understanding. Shall we discuss the script?”

“I don’t need people to follow me; I can enter it alone.”

“You misunderstand!” Cold sweat covered Liu Dao. After gathering his thoughts, he asked, “Do you truly intend to livestream alone in a place like that at midnight?”

“Is there a problem?”

Days of preparation seemed to crumble before Liu Dao’s eyes. “No, of course not. Please review the contract and tell me if you have any requests.”

He removed a provisional contract from the briefcase. Its terms were loose because this first collaboration was only a trial. Chen Ge would promote Liu Dao’s studio during his stream; in return, the studio would secure greater exposure and more platform recommendations for him.

“I’ve watched every stream. Your content is excellent, but your equipment isn’t professional.” While Chen Ge read, Liu Dao opened the briefcase and set it between them. “We can lend you this waterproof GoPro, normally used for extreme sports such as hang gliding and deep-sea diving, along with nonslip chest and arm mounts and wireless earphones. During the stream, our technicians will relay the footage, and you can monitor the broadcast on your phone.”

Liu Dao introduced each piece of equipment. “Familiarize yourself with it as soon as possible. Qin Guang hasn’t announced his next stream, but it will certainly happen within three days. We’ll schedule yours against his. The head-to-head result will decide everything.”

They were challenging the platform’s most popular host, and Liu Dao had little confidence in victory. Hence the temporary contract, which would expire after a single stream. Businesses minimized risk; Chen Ge understood that. He signed and accepted the equipment.

“I’ll contact you once Qin Guang confirms his schedule. Be ready.” Liu Dao extended his hand. “Here’s to a successful partnership—and please be careful.”

After seeing Liu Dao off, Chen Ge stored the equipment in the staff break room and returned to selling tickets. The sky darkened abruptly, and rain began around 2:00 p.m.

The rain drove away the park’s few visitors. Looking across the deserted grounds, Chen Ge’s mood sank. Haunted House attendance was rising, but the park’s overall numbers continued to fall. If New Century Park closed, his attraction would fall with it.

“The Haunted House doesn’t have enough scenarios to support the entire park.” New Century Park survived only because Jiujiang lacked competition. Once the new park opened, visitors would abandon this one.

“Boss, what’s on your mind?” Xu Wan joined him beneath an umbrella.

“Nothing really.” Chen Ge turned to look at Xu Wan. “Thank you for your work today; you can go home now. I need to go to the workshop to finish off the mannequins anyway.”

After cleaning and locking the Haunted House, Chen Ge walked to the mannequin workshop. He spotted Boss Qian squatting beside the road, chatting with a food-stall owner.

“Why are you standing outside?”

Seeing him, Boss Qian struggled to his feet. “Brother, have you reconsidered my luxury-doll proposal? I’m certain you could revolutionize the industry.”

“Not interested.” Chen Ge entered the workshop to focus on his work.

“Just think about it. You could be the next king of adult sex dolls!”

…

By 9:30 p.m., all twenty-four bodies were complete. The headless mannequins filled the workshop with a harrowing stillness.

“They’re so realistic; it’s like art.”

“I’ll leave them for the night, and I’ll come to take them tomorrow morning.” Chen Ge patted Boss Qian on his shoulder. “Watch only from afar, and please don’t touch them.”

After a few more warnings, Chen Ge left. Rain still poured outside the workshop.

How am I supposed to move twenty-four mannequins to the park? I should ask Uncle Xu for help tomorrow.He opened his umbrella and walked down the street as shopkeepers packed their wares and called their children inside.

As he passed a narrow alley, a child’s crying caught his attention. Several boys were hurling stones and empty bottles into one corner. One had a scratch on his finger and, even while sobbing, kept snatching debris from the ground to throw.

The boss of the lottery ticket shop next door came out to yell, “Jia Ming, Jia Bao, stop playing; it’s time to go home.”

“Dad, little brother was scratched by a stray cat!” one of the boys screamed.

“A cat scratched him? Let me see!” The man rushed into the alley, and after a moment’s hesitation, Chen Ge followed. At the sight of the small wound, the father embraced and comforted the child, who promptly wailed even louder.

“Don’t cry. Daddy will get revenge. Is this the cat?” He seized a brick and hurled it into the corner. It struck flesh, drawing a whimper.

Chen Ge blocked the next brick with his calf. In the corner sat a crushed cardboard box. Inside, a white cat bristled, teeth and claws bared, its body covered in bleeding wounds. Blood ran down its head, yet it refused to abandon the box.

“Why doesn’t it run?” One step closer revealed four kittens inside, none of them breathing. The boys’ debris littered the alley around the box, but the mother had kept its interior clean.

“What’s the matter with you?” The man grabbed a broom and pushed Chen Ge aside. “Move it!”

Pain still throbbed in Chen Ge’s calf. When the man shoved him, something cold surged through him. He seized the man’s arm, threw him down, and pressed his face into the mud. Chen Ge’s pupils narrowed until his stare seemed to come from beyond the grave.

Yin Yang Vision!

The man struggled at first, but one look at Chen Ge’s face froze him. His entire body shuddered, teeth chattering.

“Easy—we can talk this through.” The man dropped the broom. Face pressed into the mud, he stammered, “There are security cameras everywhere. A stray cat isn’t worth this. I’ll leave.”

Chen Ge released his grip on the man as his gaze slowly returned to normal.

“Jia Ming, Jia Bao.” The man hurried away, and the boys followed.

Silence returned to the alley. When Chen Ge approached the broken box, the injured white cat arched its back and flattened its ears. Its eyes narrowed, ready to attack.

It feared every human who came near.

Chen Ge slowly crouched, careful not to threaten it. Then he opened his umbrella and placed it over the box.
